All tests pass with -race. Done. Let me summarize concisely.

All 13 tests pass, including with the race detector enabled.

## What I implemented in `paasio.go`

The interfaces (`ReadCounter`, `WriteCounter`, `ReadWriteCounter`) were already defined in `interface.go`, so I only added the implementations:

- **`readCounter`** — wraps an `io.Reader`; `Read` delegates to the underlying reader, then under a mutex increments the byte total and operation count. `ReadCount` returns both under the same lock, so the snapshot is always consistent (required by the consistency tests, which assert `nops == n / numBytes` while other goroutines are still reading).
- **`writeCounter`** — the same pattern for `io.Writer` / `WriteCount`.
- **`readWriteCounter`** — embeds `*readCounter` and `*writeCounter` (each wrapping the same `io.ReadWriter`), so it satisfies `ReadWriteCounter` with a single mutex guarding each direction's counters.

`NewReadCounter`, `NewWriteCounter`, and `NewReadWriteCounter` construct these. Errors from the underlying reader/writer are passed through unchanged; the returned `(n, err)` is what gets counted, matching the "bytes successfully read/written" semantics in the interface docs. No new files were created and `paasio_test.go` was untouched.
